skills.name: Future reference: will, shall and present schedules

note.text: Will plus a base verb can express predictions, decisions or promises. Shall can occur with I and we in formal usage and in offers or suggestions, but it is not required in every first-person future sentence. The present simple can refer to an arranged timetable: the bus leaves tomorrow. Add a time expression when needed to make the future reference clear. Do not add -s after will or assume that every future event must use will.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Will plus a base verb can express predictions, decisions or promises. Shall can occur with I and we in formal usage and in offers or suggestions, but it is not required in every first-person future sentence. The present simple can refer to an arranged timetable: the bus leaves tomorrow. Add a time expression when needed to make the future reference clear. Do not add -s after will or assume that every future event must use will.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Bih says, I will bring the notebook. The club timetable says the meeting starts tomorrow afternoon. Ayuk asks, Shall we check the notice? These forms do different jobs: a promise, a scheduled event and a suggestion. The timetable example is fictional rather than a claim about a current transport service.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the intended function before choosing a form. Keep the base verb after will and shall. For present-simple schedules, check subject agreement and the future time expression. Avoid teaching shall as the only possible form with I or we.
